;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen]]
**The [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] launch [[ballistic missile]]s and [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]]s against [[Saudi Arabia]], including its capital [[Riyadh]]. Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki says that Saudi forces "managed to intercept and destroy" the missiles and drones. The military says that they destroyed "eight [[booby-trap]]ped unmanned aircraft [used by the Houthis] to target civilian objects and civilians in the kingdom". [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/06/saudi-coalition-shoots-houthi-ballistic-missiles-drones-200623073541760.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Somali Civil War (2009–present)]]
**Two civilians are killed after a [[suicide bombing]] occurs at a [[Turkish military]] installation in [[Mogadishu]], Turkey's largest overseas military base. [[Al-Shabaab (militant group)|Al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/06/23/world/africa/somalia-turkey-suicide-bombing.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Oaxaca earthquake]]
**A major [[earthquake]] strikes southern [[Mexico]], with its epicenter 15 miles (24.1km) northeast of [[Santa María Xadani]], [[Oaxaca]], resulting in the death of five people. It was measured at 7.4 [[Moment magnitude scale|magnitude]] and a [[tsunami warning]] was issued. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/23/weather/mexico-earthquake-southern-coast-intl/index.html (CNN)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 vaccine]]
**[[Imperial College London]] administers the first dose of their proposed COVID-19 vaccine, which is undergoing a clinical trial. [https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/198533/first-volunteer-receives-imperial-covid19-vaccine/ (Imperial College London)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**Amid increasing tensions and in spite of warnings from the [[South Korean government]], hundreds of thousands of anti-[[Kim Jong-un|Kim]] leaflets are floated across the border by a group of [[North Korean defectors]]. [https://apnews.com/7620633c882411741d16319db0fb4b58 (Associated Press)]

;Law and crime
*[[Killing of Rayshard Brooks]]
**[[Fulton County, Georgia|Fulton County]] authorities charge a woman with [[arson]] in relation to an Atlanta [[Wendy's]] restaurant being burnt down the day after [[Atlanta Police Department|police]] killed Rayshard Brooks there after he fled when they tried to arrest him for [[driving under the influence|DUI]]. The woman's lawyer said she was Brooks' girlfriend. [https://nypost.com/2020/06/23/woman-arrested-in-arson-of-wendys-where-rayshard-brooks-was-killed/ (''The New York Post'')] [https://nypost.com/2020/06/23/accused-wendys-arsonist-natalie-white-was-rayshard-brooks-girlfriend-lawyer/ (''The New York Post'')]
*A court in [[Kyrgyzstan]] sentences former [[President of Kyrgyzstan|President]] [[Almazbek Atambayev]] to 11 years in prison on [[corruption]] charges, which he denies. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-kyrgyzstan-atambayev/kyrgyz-ex-president-sentenced-to-11-years-in-prison-idUSKBN23U1CS (Reuters)]
*A court in [[Turkey]] sentences a former mayor of a [[Turkish Kurdistan|Kurdish]] city and opposition member to 16 years in prison for "being a member of a [[terrorism in Turkey|terrorist]] group, abusing power and inciting to violence and hatred". The head of a local [[human rights in Turkey|human rights]] organization says "all the charges against her are fabricated". [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/middle-east/2020/06/23/Turkish-court-sentences-former-Kurdish-mayor-to-16-years-for-inciting-violence-.html (Al Arabiya)]
*American [[Pornographic film actor|porn star]] [[Ron Jeremy]] is charged with the [[rape in the United States|rape]] of three women and [[sexual assault]] of another. [https://www.theguardian.com/society/2020/jun/23/ron-jeremy-rape-charges-los-angeles (''The Guardian'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Kiribati presidential election]]
**Incumbent [[Taneti Maamau]] is re-elected as [[President of Kiribati|President]] of [[Kiribati]] with 26,053 votes to 17,866 votes by [[Banuera Berina]], in a blow for [[Taiwan]] and its efforts to regain recognition from the Pacific country. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/419640/taneti-maamau-re-elected-president-of-kiribati-in-blow-for-taiwan (RNZ)]
*[[2020 Malawian presidential election]]
**After the results of the [[2019 Malawian general election|last general election]] in [[Malawi]] were annulled by the country's [[Judiciary of Malawi|Constitutional Court]] in February, new elections are held. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-53136963 (BBC News)]
*[[2020 Singaporean general election]]
**President [[Halimah Yacob]] dissolves Parliament and polling day is set on 10 July. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/singapore/ge2020-polling-day-jul-10-writ-of-election-issued-eld-12862530 (CNA)]
*[[2020 Kentucky Democratic presidential primary]], [[2020 United States Senate election in Kentucky]]
**Voters in Kentucky head to the polls to nominate a Democrat to face [[Party leaders of the United States Senate|Senate Majority leader]] [[Mitch McConnell]]. Former [[Vice President of the United States|Vice President]] [[Joe Biden]] also won the state primary. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/06/23/politics/kentucky-senate-democratic-primary/index.html (CNN)] [https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/503576-biden-wins-kentucky-primary (''The Hill'')] 

;Sports
*[[2020 NASCAR Cup Series]]
**[[George Floyd protests#Sports industry|George Floyd protests § Sports industry]]
***[[NASCAR]] and the [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] conclude their investigation of the [[noose]] found in the garage area of [[Bubba Wallace]], the lone African-American driver in the series, at [[Talladega Superspeedway]]. The investigation concluded the "noose" was in fact the garage door pull, and had not been touched or moved since early last fall. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/nascars-bubba-wallace-target-hate-crime-fbi-finds/story?id=71415048 (ABC News)]
